picks.title: From feedback to merged PR: making UI feedback agent-actionable
picks.excerpt: As teams wire AI coding agents (Cursor, Claude) into implementation, the shape of design feedback has to change: notes captured directly on the live app with page URLs, element selectors, screenshots, and viewport context can be converted straight into pull requests without a human translation step. A concrete look at agentic design-to-code handoff — how design critique becomes machine-actionable rather than a Figma comment or Slack thread.
picks.rationale: Reframes how design feedback reaches code: notes captured on the live app with selectors and viewport context become pull requests directly, no human translation step. Changes the design-to-code handoff a team runs tomorrow.

picks.title: Why Do AI-Generated Websites All Look the Same?
picks.excerpt: AI website builders now ship clean, responsive code, yet the output converges on the same visual signatures — glassmorphism, identical hero layouts, standardized card grids. The piece argues models reproduce common patterns rather than truly design, a pointed 'AI slop' critique of homogenized generative UI and what it means for brand differentiation and design taste.
picks.rationale: Names the design cost of generative UI: builders converge on glassmorphism, identical heroes, and standard card grids because models reproduce patterns instead of designing. A taste-and-differentiation read every design team wrestling with AI tools needs. Distinct accent from the other workflow pick.

picks.title: Hate generative AI? Maybe it's time to boycott Netflix
picks.excerpt: With Netflix leaning into generative AI across its productions, Creative Bloq argues creatives angry about AI's encroachment on craft should vote with their subscriptions. It's a look at how a major studio's gen-AI adoption reshapes creative and design work and the leverage audiences and practitioners still hold — a culture-and-craft read on the design/creative industry's AI backlash.
picks.rationale: The culture-and-craft angle on the AI backlash: a major studio's gen-AI push and the leverage practitioners and audiences still hold. Adds an industry-context read alongside the tool and workflow picks. Distinct accent from the other workflow cards.
